relevance_note: The paper sequences ABC1 in three named Tangier disease patients: "Different mutations were detected in the ABC1 gene of 3 unrelated patients" (TD1, TD2, TD3), with per-patient variants and zygosity.
method_note: Read in full by hand; JSON assembled with a short Python script from values chosen while reading. Scope: three patients with homozygous TD (TD1, TD2, TD3); two normal (non-TD) fibroblast donors are out of scope (cohort_size_as_stated counts the 3 TD patients only). No relatives are described. Labels TD1-TD3 are the paper's own; TD1 and TD2 were previously described as TG2 and TG1 (ref 10), and TD1 = TD-2 of ref. 36. Variants are printed only as prose (no HGVS): TD1 Gln537Arg (A to G), homozygous; TD2 Arg527Trp plus an undetermined defect on the second allele (kept as a 'not reported' variant row); TD3 a 14-nt insertion after nucleotide 5697 and a 138-bp insertion after nucleotide 5062. No transcript is stated for the patient variants; the Methods give GenBank AJ012376 numbering only for the normal-sequence differences, so transcript_as_stated is 'not reported'. Variant type 'missense' for TD1/TD2 rests on the paper's 'substitution altering the charge of an amino acid'; the TD3 138-bp insertion is typed 'other' (insertion containing an in-frame stop codon). The phrase 'homozygous TD' is the paper's disease label for all three, although TD2 and TD3 are stated to be compound heterozygotes. Individual clinical data are given only for TD3 (age 18 at cell sampling recorded as age at last evaluation, sex, orange tonsil remnants, asymmetrical motor neuropathy, HDL 5 mg/dL, LDL 16 mg/dL). Low HDL and low LDL checklist items for TD3 were marked observed from these numeric values, which the paper does not itself label as low. 'Tonsil remnants' was not taken to state a tonsillectomy (checklist left not reported). Cellular efflux defects are recorded as functional evidence, not phenotypic features. Population screening ('Neither of the substitution mutations was found in more than 80 alleles') is not an author classification and was not recorded as pathogenicity. No contradictions found.
